sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Besides windows, doors and ventilators, ______ should be installed in the kitchen to remove stale air. (ii) Chances of infections and fungal diseases increase if the rooms are ______. (iii) The floor of a bathroom should be ______. (iv) The living room should be near the ______ of the building.
questions.answer: (i) an exhaust fan. (ii) dark and damp. (iii) non-slippery. (iv) entrance.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Removing cobwebs is a daily activity. (ii) Safe disposal of excreta helps to keep our environment healthy. (iii) Cross ventilation is achieved by placing two windows on opposite walls. (iv) A rocky surface is good for the foundation of a house as it absorbs water.
questions.answer: (i) False – it is a weekly activity. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – rocky surface is good for the foundation but does not absorb water.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Besides sanitation, two other aspects of maintaining hygiene in houses are ______ and ______. (ii) To make your house more spacious combine the kitchen with ______ and ______ room.

State True or False: (i) Sulabh sauchalaya are environment friendly. (ii) Soakage pits should be 1 metre deep and 2 metres wide. (iii) Sunlight acts as a mild disinfectant. (iv) Indoor plants turn yellow in brightly lit rooms.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – a suitable pit is about 2 m deep and 1 m wide. (iii) True. (iv) False – they wither in dark rooms.
questions.note: April 2024 asked this as an assertion-reason: Sulabh sauchalaya are eco-friendly because they need only 1.5 to 2 litres of water for flushing – both true.

questions.q: Match the function of a home with the activity: (A) Celebrating Diwali (B) Keeping a paying guest (C) Caring of children and old people (D) Learning to respect others; (i) Educative (ii) Economic (iii) Protective (iv) Social/religious.
Match the cleaning activity with the type: (A) Dusting (B) Cleaning bathrooms (C) Washing curtains (D) Cleaning before Diwali; (i) Weekly (ii) Seasonal (iii) Daily.

Match the site feature with the situation: (A) Area with water, electricity, roads (B) Loose soil (C) Elevated land (D) Bank and market nearby; (i) Soil (ii) Physical features (iii) Practical convenience (iv) Neighbourhood.

State True or False: (i) Soakage pits are suitable where there is no drainage system. (ii) A pit latrine is ideal for permanent use. (iii) Waste water should be allowed to stagnate near the house. (iv) Segregate bio-degradable and non-bio-degradable waste.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – only for temporary use. (iii) False. (iv) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write any four educational functions of a house.
questions.answer: It teaches basic values like respect for elders, love and affection, religion, discipline and responsibility; life skills like sharing, caring and empathy; health habits; and transfers customs and values from generation to generation.

or.q: List any four household activities that are done once a week in your home.
or.answer: Cleaning bathrooms and toilets; removing cobwebs; cleaning kitchen shelves; cleaning door handles; polishing wooden surfaces; cleaning washbasins and metal objects.

questions.q: Analyse any two common mistakes in selecting a bedroom.
questions.answer: Choosing a noisy room with no privacy; an odd shape that cannot hold beds and furniture; no attached bathroom; poor light and ventilation.

questions.q: What two points each should be considered while making a bathroom and bedroom?
questions.answer: Bathroom: non-slippery easy-to-clean floor; at least one wall exposed to the outside for light and air. Bedroom: privacy and freedom from noise; rectangular shape; attached bathroom.

or.q: What is the ideal direction for a kitchen? What other three aspects should be considered while making it?
or.answer: East or north-east for morning sunlight. Also: good drainage and wire-mesh doors, adequate light and exhaust fan with cross ventilation, adequate storage above and below the counter.

questions.q: Apart from soap and water, what materials are used for washing tiles, plastic buckets and metal taps in the bathroom?
questions.answer: Tiles: commercial tile cleaners, vinegar, mild hydrochloric acid. Plastic buckets: scrubber, vinegar, kerosene and soda (avoid hard cleaners). Metal taps: lemon, vinegar, tamarind and salt.

questions.q: Why is it important to ensure enough light and air circulation in a house? Give two reasons each.
questions.answer: Light: kills germs and keeps rooms dry so mosquitoes and fungus do not breed; helps in work and prevents eye strain. Air: removes smoke, smell and moisture; fresh air is essential for health and prevents stuffiness.

questions.q: Why is cleanliness of the house and its surroundings important?
questions.answer: Clean surroundings keep insects and germs away; dust spreads diseases; it prevents infections, saves the house from damage and makes it pleasant to live in.

questions.q: Suggest two ways of making provisions for light in a house.
questions.answer: Provide windows, ventilators and skylights so that most rooms get sunlight; use proper artificial lighting (tube light, bulbs) that falls on the work and not on the eyes.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What are six advantages of making a toilet based on septic tanks?
questions.answer: It is hygienic; low cost and easy to construct compared with the water-closet system; does not pollute surface or ground water; free from foul smell; needs only 1.5–2 litres of water for flushing against 13–14 litres in a flush toilet; needs no cleaning of pits and the sludge is good manure; also eliminates mosquitoes, insects and fly breeding.

or.q: What six points should be kept in mind to ensure the rooms in your house do not get dirty?
or.answer: Use special indoor footwear and foot mats; fit fine wire mesh on doors and windows; keep things in their places; do daily, weekly and seasonal cleaning properly; keep dustbins covered and empty them daily; avoid bringing in dust, and dispose of waste water and garbage properly.

questions.q: Analyse any six possible mistakes families make while selecting a bedroom.
questions.answer: Choosing a room that is noisy or lacks privacy; badly lit or poorly ventilated; too small or odd-shaped to place beds and furniture; far from the bathroom; near the kitchen or the entrance; ignoring storage; too much furniture; not considering that one-third of life is spent sleeping.

questions.q: Write any six features on the basis of which you will select the site for your new house.
questions.answer: Developed neighbourhood with electricity, roads and drainage; open area away from heavy traffic; not low-lying (no flooding or water-logging); firm soil 2–5 feet below the surface; not a garbage-filled plot; markets, transport, bank, post office and hospital within walking distance; matching the family's social and economic status.

or.q: Give six suggestions to make your house more comfortable.
or.answer: List activities of each room and mark space; combine activities (dining with kitchen); avoid overcrowding; use multipurpose furniture; use furniture for storage and as room dividers; use space below the staircase; light colours on walls; ensure light and ventilation.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the functions of a home with examples (any five points).
questions.answer: (1) Protective: gives security and shelter from weather, animals and enemies. (2) Economic: has a money value, raises socio-economic status and pride, and can be used for income-generating activity (tuitions, paying guest). (3) Educative: teaches values such as respect and discipline and life skills like sharing and caring. (4) Social/religious: promotes interaction within and outside the family and a sense of belongingness. (5) Transfers values and customs from generation to generation, celebrates festivals together.

questions.q: Describe the methods of safe disposal of human excreta in villages and towns.
questions.answer: Water closet: excreta carried by flush through drains and sewers, the most sanitary but needs plenty of water and is expensive. Septic tank: concrete tank connected to household drains, hygienic, low cost, needs only 1.5–2 litres of water, no foul smell, sludge is manure (Sulabh Shauchalaya). Pit latrine: pit more than 3 m deep in sandy soil with a lid, for temporary use; not very hygienic because it can pollute ground water. Soakage pits take waste water where no drainage exists.
